clue.text: Keen to enter theatre, make parts of journey by lorry

parts.note: stages are the separate legs or parts of a journey
a truck is a lorry, the British word for a heavy goods vehicle

explanation.surface: A traveller covers a journey in legs, hitching rides on a lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone smitten with a longing to act on the stage is keen to go into the theatre.

clue.text: The very man to hold theological discussion?

definitions.meaning: the idiom is said when the person just mentioned walks in: here he is, the man himself
read literally, the phrase means discussing Satan, a theological topic

explanation.surface: Someone is wanted to lead a debate on religion.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom greets the arrival of the very person under discussion; read literally it means discussing Satan.

clue.text: Develop good argument

parts.note: a row is a quarrel or argument

explanation.definitionFit: To develop is to increase in size or maturity, a synonym.

clue.text: Observes sailors to be dazed

parts.note: to observe is to see, so observes gives sees
tars is an old slang word for sailors

explanation.surface: A captain watches his crew reel about in a stupor.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: after a blow to the head one is dizzy and glimpses flashes of light.

clue.text: Working by going round charitable club

definitions.meaning: the ... Club is an international service and charity organisation

explanation.surface: A charity club gets its work done by touring the district.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotary describes motion by rotation, and Rotary International is a well-known charitable club.

clue.text: He may make some quiche fashionable

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cook might turn quiche into a trendy dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook in a kitchen is the person who would make a quiche.

clue.text: Hood fortress, we worked out

indicators.note: worked out says the preceding words are rearranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Merry men deduce where their leader Robin Hood keeps his stronghold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' rearranges HOOD FORTRESS WE; the whole clue is also the definition, as the woodland was the outlaw Robin Hood's legendary base.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend makes the Nottinghamshire woodland the refuge and stronghold of the outlaw Robin Hood.

clue.text: Orator's joint office in Commons

parts.note: an orator is a speaker, with its possessive
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A speechmaker shares a room in Parliament with a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: The Speaker chairs debates in the House of Commons, the elected chamber of the UK Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The role of presiding officer of the House of Commons is a parliamentary post.

clue.text: Finished with retailing-so disorganised

parts.note: something finished is all over
retailing is done in the shop

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper closes down, the business in chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal idiom: scattered everywhere, in a muddle, without order.

clue.text: Twice as frank? The truth's so misleading

parts.note: twice as much is double
bluff means blunt or frank in manner

explanation.surface: Someone extra candid is wrongly suspected of lying.
explanation.walkthrough: In this ploy you tell the truth expecting the listener to assume you are deceiving them.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruse in which honesty itself deceives, because the hearer expects a lie.

clue.text: Bachelor in spectacles with English pipe

indicators.note: in says the bachelor's letter sits inside the spectacles

parts.note: OO pictures a pair of glasses

explanation.surface: A single Englishman in glasses smokes a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind instrument is a kind of pipe, in crossword usage.

clue.text: Not much in teacup?

parts.note: the idiom of a great fuss over nothing is this weather event in a teacup, so not much of one fits there

explanation.definitionFit: A tempest in a cup of tea is a fuss about very little, a famous idiom.

clue.text: Drivers circled about district

indicators.note: circled means the drivers' letters go round the other piece

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Motorists drive round and round a neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A district is a region or zone, a synonym.

clue.text: We hear it made a report on the slide

indicators.note: we hear says the word is said aloud and written differently

parts.note: to shoot is to fire a gun, which makes a report or bang

explanation.surface: A rumour spread that someone had written up an account of the playground slide.
explanation.definitionFit: A playground or water slide is a synonym.

clue.text: I'm not certain if I have one

definitions.text: I'm not certain if I have one

parts.words: I'm not certain if I have one
parts.note: having one of these is the very state of uncertainty, so the speaker is unsure

explanation.definitionFit: Uncertainty is exactly the feeling of not being sure.

clue.text: Kills with this look?

explanation.surface: A murderer's glance could slay.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang replaces a word with a rhyming phrase and then drops the rhyme: 'have a butcher's' means take a look.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher is to slaughter; in rhyming slang a butcher's is a look.

clue.text: Complain about fine for Aussie flyer

indicators.note: about means the first piece is wrapped round the second

parts.note: to mope is to sulk and grumble
OK means fine or all right

explanation.surface: A tourist moans about a penalty incurred while flying to Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: An Australian owl, a native bird, so a flyer from down under.

clue.text: Piano piece, a tiny thing

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
an article is a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A short composition for piano is only a little item.
explanation.definitionFit: A minute fragment or speck of matter, a synonym.

clue.text: With level time, second in athletics contests

parts.note: level means even

explanation.surface: An athlete finishes level on time and comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: Competitions at a sports meeting, such as the hurdles, are the separate fixtures on the programme.

clue.text: Wounding remarks hold trouble for holiday island

indicators.note: hold means the remarks contain the trouble inside them

parts.note: barbs are cutting, hurtful comments
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Insults cause a row on a Caribbean vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caribbean island popular with tourists, a resort destination.

clue.text: A daily glass

explanation.surface: Someone checks their reflection every day.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of a British newspaper, and a looking-glass.

clue.text: Stagger back, getting malicious look

indicators.note: back says the word for stagger is read in reverse

parts.note: to reel is to stagger

explanation.surface: Someone reels backwards on receiving a nasty glare.
explanation.definitionFit: A sly, lecherous or spiteful sideways glance.

clue.text: Show of godliness, putting energy into compassion

indicators.note: putting into means one letter goes inside the word for compassion

parts.note: pity is compassion
E is the physics abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: A charitable act shows real religious fervour.
explanation.definitionFit: Devoutness and reverence for God, a synonym for religious devotion.

clue.text: Bear to be meditation devotee

definitions.meaning: a Hindu ascetic who practises meditation

explanation.surface: A bear takes up meditation.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous cartoon bear, and a master of meditation.

clue.text: Footwear's sound, so buzz off

indicators.note: the word sound signals the footwear word is said aloud

parts.note: a shoe is an item of footwear

explanation.surface: Squeaky shoes drive someone away.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation telling someone to go away.

clue.text: Three people involved in riot

indicators.note: involved in suggests the letters of riot are tangled up

explanation.surface: A trio is caught up in a public disturbance.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of three, a set of three performers.

clue.text: Behind stairs, judge found black box

indicators.note: behind places the judge after the stairs in the answer

parts.note: a flight of stairs
a recorder is a part-time judge in England

explanation.surface: A magistrate found a mysterious box under the staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockpit data device on an aircraft, nicknamed a black box.

clue.text: Burn out home — moving to this town?

indicators.note: moving says the letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone burnt out by home life moves to a seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Anagram of BURN OUT HOME; the resort is on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside resort town in Dorset on England's south coast.
